correctness.rationale: Direct substitution of u,v into the ell_4 norming functional produces a union of centered ellipses with axes a_s=sqrt(s)/(2-s), b_s=sqrt(s(1-s))/(2-s). The squared directional support is H_q(s)=s(1-q s)/(2-s)^2 with derivative (2+s(1-4q))/(2-s)^3; its max switches at q=3/4. For any fixed |x|<1, squared obtainable ordinates G_x(s)=(1-s)(s/(2-s)^2-x^2) form a continuous filled vertical interval with a unique positive maximum; its optimizing equation gives the stated x(s),y(s) boundary. The boundary slope decreases strictly, implying concavity, hence actual W convex rather than only its hull. Direct exact integration gives the area and minimum support the inradius; endpoint coordinate-zero cases included. Independent 51 checks include angular maximization and area quadrature and do not prove continuum assertions.

value.rationale: The fundamental two-coordinate permutation isometry on the first non-Hilbert even exponent is a natural benchmark for spatial Banach numerical range geometry. An exact support-angle transition, nonobvious convexity and a closed planar area measure quantify deformation from the Hilbert interval.

final_claim: For F(u,v)=(v,u) on complex ell_4^2 with the normalized spatial duality map, the actual numerical range is convex, has support h(phi)=|cos phi| for sin^2 phi<=3/4 and h(phi)=1/sqrt(8(2sin^2 phi-1)) otherwise, an explicitly parametrized fourfold-symmetric boundary, exact area 3sqrt(3)/8+3 log(2+sqrt(3))/16, and centered inradius 1/(2sqrt2).
limitations: Only the spatial numerical range for F on complex ell_4^2 and its affine translates/scalings.
Area and inradius are for actual W(F), not arbitrary numerical-range convex hulls.
